title: A Letter for the Inheritance
premise: Yara Okafor, a night-shift dispatcher who has never failed to close a case, receives two letters addressed to him: one confessing to a murder committed thirty years ago, the other promising a fortune if he can find 'the ledger that was never written.' Following the confession's clues through the city's taxi routes, Yara discovers the ledger is encoded in decades of dispatch records — and that his own late father, once a driver for the same company, appears in its margins. The inheritance isn't money but the truth: the confessor, dying company matriarch Ada Voss, killed her business partner to protect Yara's father from being framed. In the end, Yara must choose between publishing the truth that would destroy Voss's family — who have quietly funded his life — or honoring loyalty by letting the ledger burn; he chooses truth, but delivers it only to the one person it can still save.
about_author: Cyrus Ishikawa is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent six years listening to a city talk back through a radio headset. They write mysteries about people whose jobs are invisible until the night everything depends on them.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Address
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. During a slow night shift, Yara receives two letters: a typed confession to a 1994 murder signed with no name, and a second letter offering an inheritance contingent on finding 'the unwritten ledger.' The emotional beat is wary curiosity — Yara's pride in closing every case pulls him in before he decides to accept.

chapters.title: The Route That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. The confession references a taxi route discontinued decades ago. Digging into company archives, Yara finds dispatch logs with gaps — pages cut out cleanly. He notices his father's name on an old driver roster. Beat: unease deepening into personal stakes as the case stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Ada Voss's Long Goodbye
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara traces the letters' postmark to the Voss estate, where dying matriarch Ada Voss receives him with unsettling familiarity — she knows his name, his father's name. She neither confirms nor denies, only says: 'The ledger is where you've been looking all along.' Beat: dread wrapped in hospitality.

chapters.title: Margins and Mileage
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Cross-referencing old fare ledgers against route maps, Yara realizes the numbers encode dates, payments, and initials — a hidden accounting of blackmail. His father's initials recur beside large sums received. Beat: betrayal's first sting; Yara questions everything he believed about his father.

chapters.title: The Son Who Drives Like His Father
chapters.summary: POV: Marcus Voss. Ada's son Marcus, desperate to protect the family name, begins shadowing Yara, convinced he's a blackmailer. A tense confrontation at a depot reveals Marcus knows about the confession too — and wants the letters destroyed. Beat: open antagonism; the hunt becomes mutual.

chapters.title: What the Radio Remembered
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. A retired dispatcher, Sal, recalls the night of the murder: two drivers left the depot, only one came back. Yara reconstructs the timeline and realizes his father wasn't the killer — he was being framed, and someone paid to bury the evidence. Beat: grief transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Burn Before Morning
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Someone ransacks the archive room and steals the key ledgers; Yara barely rescues the coded pages he'd copied. A threatening note makes clear how far the family will go. Beat: fear and isolation — Yara realizes finishing this case may cost him everything, including safety.

chapters.title: The Confession's Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Forensic attention to the confession reveals two hands wrote it: Ada's words, amended by another. Yara confronts Ada on her deathbed; she finally tells the whole story — she killed her partner to stop him framing Yara's father, then spent thirty years paying silence. Beat: devastating clarity; the mystery's moral weight lands.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Marcus, learning the truth, offers Yara money to burn the ledger — the same choice Ada made. Yara refuses both bribe and destruction, but instead of going public, he gives the decoded ledger to the one living person wronged besides his father: the victim's estranged daughter. Beat: climax of principle over profit.

chapters.title: Last Call
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Ada dies peacefully; Marcus, stripped of leverage, chooses not to pursue revenge. Yara closes the case file — his first case he resolves without an arrest, only an accounting. On his next shift, a new letter arrives. He smiles, files it under 'pending.' Beat: bittersweet resolution; truth delivered, loyalty honored, identity reclaimed.
